senses.definition: A continuous humming noise, as of bees; a confused murmur, as of general conversation in low tones.

quotes.text: Immediately there was a ringing and a singing in the hills, and then a whispering and a lisping and a whiz and a buzz all about him, for the little people were now some whirling round and round in the dance, and others sporting and tumbling about in the moonshine, and playing a thousand merry pranks and tricks.

senses.definition: The audible friction of voiced consonants.

examples: Still feeling the buzz from the coffee, he pushed through the last of the homework.

senses.definition: (colloquial) To show a high level of activity and haste, energization or excitement, to be busy as a bee in one’s actions but perhaps mentally charged.
(transitive) To whisper; to communicate, as tales, in an undertone; to spread, as a report, by whispers or secretly.

quotes.text: I will buzz abroad such prophecies / That Edward shall be fearful of his life.
